string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of its four direct-administered municipalities. It is the country\'s political, cultural, and educational centre, hosting the headquarters of most major state institutions. The city has a history spanning more than three thousand years, with landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, and the Temple of Heaven attracting millions of visitors each year. As the host of the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games, Beijing is also a modern global city with advanced transport, technology, and business districts. Its population exceeds twenty million, making it one of the most populous cities in the world.

Shanghai is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities and the country\'s largest city by population. Located on the east coast at the mouth of the Yangtze River, it is a global financial, trade, and shipping hub. The Bund, with its historic European buildings, contrasts with the futuristic skyscrapers of the Pudong district, including the iconic Shanghai Tower. The city\'s port is the busiest container port in the world, and its stock exchange is among the most important in Asia. Shanghai combines a rich cultural heritage with rapid innovation, attracting millions of domestic and international visitors every year.

Chongqing is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities and the only one located deep in the western part of the country. Situated in a mountainous area where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet, it is known as the Mountain City for its dramatic hillside buildings and layered streets. Chongqing is an important industrial, transport, and logistics centre, serving as a gateway to western China. The city is famous for its spicy hotpot cuisine, night-time scenery, and the historic Dazu Rock Carvings, a UNESCO World Heritage site. With a population of over thirty million, it is one of the largest municipalities in the world.

Tianjin is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities, located on the coast near Beijing in the north of the country. It is an important port city and a major hub for manufacturing, shipping, and foreign trade. Tianjin has a unique mix of Chinese and Western architecture, reflecting its history as a treaty port in the nineteenth century, with landmarks such as the Tianjin Eye Ferris wheel and the Five Great Avenues area. The city is also known for its traditional crafts, including painted clay figurines, and its local snacks such as Goubuli stuffed buns. Tianjin continues to develop as a modern industrial and innovation centre serving northern China.
